On 18 February 1911 an earthquake in the Pamir mountains of today's Tajikistan brought down a whole mountainside into the valley of the Murghab River. About 2 cubic kilometres of rock buried the village of Usoi with its people and blocked the river with the tallest dam on Earth, natural or man-made, about 567 metres high.

Behind it the river slowly filled the valley, forming Lake Sarez, about 55 km long and up to 500 metres deep. The dam has held for more than a century, with water seeping through it instead of spilling over the top.

Scientists worry that another earthquake, or a landslide into the lake, could send a flood down the Bartang and Panj valleys toward the Amu Darya, where millions of people live, and a warning system now watches the dam. The quake came weeks after the Kebin earthquake in the Tian Shan. For a man-made dam in the same mountains, see the Nurek Dam.
